Legal Restrictions on Automated Shopping Bots

E-commerce platform eBay has imposed restrictions on third-party automation tools and AI-powered shopping bots through an update to its user agreement. The company is specifically targeting “buy for me” agents—which can place orders without human intervention—and LLM-based bots.

This technology, known in the industry as “agentic commerce,” autonomously searches for, compares, and purchases products on behalf of users. eBay’s updated policy explicitly prohibits the unauthorized use of end-to-end workflows that lack human oversight. The new terms will take effect on February 20, 2026.

Transition from the Robots.txt File to the User Agreement

eBay had previously imposed technical restrictions on bots from companies such as Perplexity, Anthropic, and Amazon through the robots.txt to impose technical barriers on bots from companies such as Perplexity, Anthropic, and Amazon. However, this file was merely advisory in nature and had limited legal enforceability. Including the ban directly in the user agreement grants the company the right to take legal action against those who violate the rules.

These restrictions on the platform cover the following areas:

  • Autonomous order flows without human oversight.
  • Unauthorized data scraping tools.
  • External LLM-based shopping assistants.

The company stated that this ban does not apply to collaborations with eBay that have been previously approved. This suggests that official integrations with OpenAI or similar AI companies may be possible in the future. Additionally, eBay continues to test internal AI solutions within its own search and shopping infrastructure.
